final_candidates.decision_summary: RING-domain Zn-ligand cysteine with very high LOF phenotype (0.992) and good MSA applicability (0.80). Tyr substitution abolishes zinc coordination while the aromatic side chain can pack into the fold.
Conserved RING Zn-ligand histidine with the highest phenotype score (0.998) and strong MSA coverage (0.96). Alanine is minimally structurally perturbing, best balancing LOF with folding preservation.
RING Zn-ligand cysteine with phenotype 0.997 and the highest natural evolutionary tolerance among disruptive candidates (z=0.215), supporting retention of overall fold despite functional ablation.

stop_reason.detail: Evidence across phenotype and MSA tools is consistent and saturated; residual ordering differences are below the resolution of the available tools.

history.rationale: RING domain Zn2+-coordinating cysteine; substitution with bulky Tyr disrupts the zinc-binding fold required for E3 ubiquitin ligase activity and BARD1 interaction, a classic LOF mechanism.
RING-domain zinc-coordinating cysteine; Tyr substitution disrupts Zn2+ coordination and E3 ubiquitin ligase activity, a classic LOF mechanism.
AlphaMissense 0.992 and zero evolutionary tolerance at a RING Zn-ligating cysteine; C61Y is a known cancer germline LOF mutation.

Highest-confidence RING zinc-ligand substitution with strong phenotype (0.992) and good MSA applicability (0.80); low rules-fallback plm score reflects expected disruptive chemistry, which aligns with LOF intent.
Second Zn-ligating cysteine of the RING domain; Tyr substitution abolishes metal coordination, abolishing tumor-suppressor function with documented pathogenic impact.
Second RING Zn-coordinating cysteine; Tyr disrupts the RING fold's metal-binding loop and abolishes ligase function.
Phenotype 0.993 with 0.01 mutant frequency in homologs at another RING Zn-ligating cysteine.
Strong phenotype (0.993) and highest MSA coverage (0.94); remains Top-3 caliber alongside C61Y, though slightly behind on folding-preservation versus C64R/H41A.
Found BRCA1 missense variant in the BRCT domain that disrupts the phospho-peptide binding pocket and BRIP1/Abraxas interactions; strong LOF with retained overall fold (missense, not truncating).
C-terminal BRCT domain; Met1775Arg is a known pathogenic BRCT destabilizing substitution that abolishes phospho-peptide binding while retaining fold. Will verify with phenotype tool next round.
Canonical BRCT destabilizing mutation with phenotype 0.893; slightly lower than RING candidates but strong clinical precedent.
Canonical BRCT pathogenic hotspot with phenotype 0.893, but MSA applicability is near zero (0.04), leaving homolog support unverified; held as backup below RING candidates.
BRCT domain residue contacting pSer/pTyr ligands; Trp substitution perturbs the phospho-recognition groove, impairing DNA-repair scaffolding while keeping the domain folded.
BRCT phospho-peptide binding pocket residue; Trp substitution disrupts BRCA1 interaction with Abraxas/BACH1/RAP80 partners.
Lowest phenotype score in the pool (0.824) and no MSA support; dominated by other BRCT and RING candidates.

rejection.reason: Lowest phenotype score in the pool (0.824) and no MSA support; dominated by other BRCT and RING candidates.

history.rationale: RING Zn-ligand cysteine; Ser cannot coordinate zinc, abolishing E3 ligase activity; conservative size change limits gross misfolding.
RING Zn-ligand Ser substitution removes metal coordination with modest structural impact.
Highest phenotype score (0.996) at a RING Zn-ligand, though S appears in ~11% of homologs, slightly weakening evolutionary-disruption support.
Phenotype 0.996 and the only substitution with nonzero MSA natural tolerance (0.111), but Cys->Ser retains some Zn-ligation capacity, so slightly weaker LOF certainty.
BRCT repeat interface residue; Phe substitution distorts the phospho-peptide binding surface, a known deleterious BRCA1 variant class.
BRCT-region missense with reported pathogenic association; pending evidence verification.
Phenotype 0.894 only at a non-catalytic linker position; superseded by stronger candidates.

rejection.reason: Phenotype 0.894 only at a non-catalytic linker position; superseded by stronger candidates.

history.rationale: BRCT pocket residue involved in phosphoserine recognition; Lys charge reversal disrupts ligand binding and DNA-repair signaling.
BRCT pocket-adjacent position; charged substitution may disrupt partner binding.
Moderate phenotype 0.935; below the RING cysteine cluster for both score and mechanism.
Phenotype 0.935 is solid but MSA applicability 0.04 and it is dominated by six candidates with stronger, better-corroborated evidence at catalytic/domain positions.

rejection.reason: Phenotype 0.935 is solid but MSA applicability 0.04 and it is dominated by six candidates with stronger, better-corroborated evidence at catalytic/domain positions.

history.rationale: RING zinc-ligating histidine; Ala removes metal coordination, abolishing ligase function via a small substitution less likely to unfold the domain.
RING Zn-ligand histidine; Ala removes coordination but is fold-minimal.
Phenotype 0.998 and near-zero (0.0099) homolog tolerance at the RING Zn-ligating His.
Highest phenotype score (0.998) at a conserved RING Zn-ligand histidine with strong MSA coverage (0.96); Alanine substitution is minimally structurally perturbing.
BRCT surface residue contributing to partner recognition; charge reversal disrupts tumor-suppressor interactions without gross structural disruption.
BRCT surface charge reversal; plausible interaction disruption, lower prior confidence.
Phenotype 0.960 at a BRCT phosphopeptide-binding residue; MSA applicability too low for evolutionary support.
Good phenotype (0.960) but poor MSA applicability and best plm score, suggesting charge-swap may be tolerated; retained but below RING/BRCT hotspots.
RING Zn-ligand cysteine near the E2/BARD1 interface; Arg substitution eliminates zinc coordination and abolishes ubiquitin-ligase activity.
RING Zn-ligand cysteine; Arg may destabilize local fold more than needed, pending evidence.
High phenotype 0.997 but R occurs in 21% of homologs at position 64, so functional disruption is less certain.

Cys64 is a RING Zn-ligand with phenotype 0.997 and, uniquely, some natural evolutionary tolerance (z=0.215), best satisfying 'LOF while preserving folding' constraint; plm=0 is a low-reliability rules signal.
